newsitem.title: USA: KCBT wheat ends higher on mill buying, option play.
newsitem.headline: KCBT wheat ends higher on mill buying, option play.

text.p: KCBT hard red winter wheat futures settled higher on mill buying in the March contract, and traders cited mill action in wheat options as a supportive factor in the July futures contract.

"Kansas City followed Minneapolis higher today. Strength in our March was on mill-buying by General Mills," a trader said. "Strength in July came as mill interests bought the July future but at the same time put on an options program that bought KCBT July $3.70 calls and $3.10 puts."
Traders said it appeared the mills were starting to take coverage in the new crop.
Some position squaring was noted before the release Wednesday of USDA's February supply/demand report.
Short covering on signals the wheat market was oversold was cited as a key supportive influence with exports quiet and there were no weather issues to stir trading interest.
KCBT wheat settled 1-1/2 to 2-1/2 cents per bushel higher, with March up 1-1/2 cents at $4.14. July gained one cent to close at $3.54.
